title: Lattice location of ion-implanted $^{6}\mathrm{He}$ in diamond
summary: Understanding the properties of helium in diamond is crucial for geological dating and possible quantum applications. Here, the authors determine the lattice location of ion-implanted short-lived He in single-crystal diamond at temperatures from 30°C to 800°C using the β emission channeling technique. He preferentially occupies tetrahedral interstitial sites. From the temperature dependence of the interstitial fraction, the migration energy of He is estimated at 1.63–2.89 eV, implying unbound interstitial helium is unstable in diamond over geological timescales, an important insight to be considered in He-based dating methods.
